blocks.h2: Emergency Plumbing Questions From Hinsdale Homeowners

items.answer: Yes. Our phone line is open around the clock, including weekends and holidays.

items.q: What should I do while I wait?
items.preview: Shut off the water and stay safe.
items.answer: For a leak, close the main water valve. For a backup, stop using water. Stay away from electrical outlets near the water.

items.q: Where is the main water shutoff in an older home?
items.preview: Usually in the basement at the front wall.
items.answer: In most Hinsdale homes, it's in the basement where the water line comes in from the street, often on the front wall near the meter.

items.q: Will an emergency visit cost more?
items.preview: You'll see the price before work begins.
items.answer: You'll get a flat-rate price before any work begins, so you know the cost going in.

items.q: How quickly can you get here?
items.answer: Arrival times depend on the day and the weather, but we'll get a plumber to you as soon as we can.

items.q: Water is coming through the ceiling. What do I do?
items.preview: Shut off the main valve and the power to that area.
items.answer: Shut off the main water valve right away and turn off power to any lights or fixtures near the leak. Then call us.

items.q: What if my sump pump fails during a storm?
items.answer: Call us right away. In the meantime, check power and the float.
